channel.title: Oncogenic remodeling of the translational landscape uncouples hyperproliferation from ribosomal biogenesis in Ewing sarcoma
channel.description: Abstract Rapid cellular proliferation is typically sustained by hyperactive protein translation and robust ribosome production. Consistent with this, chronic ribosome biogenesis deficiency has primarily been associated with impaired growth and quiescent cellular states. Whether highly proliferative cells can adapt to persistent limitations in ribosome production and sustain growth under these conditions remains poorly understood. Ewing sarcoma provides a compelling model of this paradox. Despite its aggressive and highly proliferative nature, Ewing sarcoma is characterized by remarkably small nucleoli, a longstanding histopathological hallmark suggestive of constitutively reduced nucleolar output. Here, we use Ewing sarcoma to investigate how rapidly proliferating cells adapt to chronic limitation of ribosome availability. We show that EWSR1::FLI1, the main oncogenic fusion protein driving Ewing sarcoma, interferes with the RNA-binding protein EWSR1, impairing R-loop clearance at rDNA loci. R-loop accumulation drives aberrant UBF1 aggregation and nucleolar reorganization, leading to a global reduction in rRNA and protein synthesis. Ribosome-fraction proteomics and polysome sequencing reveal that, in response to this ribosome shortage, cells rewire their translational machinery: loading of initiation factor eIF3 onto free 40S subunits is reduced, while polysomes preferentially engage ribosomal protein and other 5′TOP transcripts, maintaining ribosomal stoichiometry despite critically reduced rRNA availability. Rather than enhancing ribosome production, rapidly dividing cells thus respond to biosynthetic constraints by redirecting their limited translational resources. However, by operating at the limit of their biosynthetic capacity, these cells retain no buffer to absorb further translational stress. We show that exposure to additional nucleolar insults or genotoxic damage triggers a rapid, SLFN11-dependent suppression of protein synthesis and apoptosis – a direct consequence of EWSR1::FLI1 expression.

item.title: Nucleolus imaging
item.description: We applied confocal and super-resolution STED microscopy to dissect nucleolar organization and ribosome biogenesis in Ewing sarcoma. Confocal imaging enables quantitative assessment of nucleolar size based on UBF1 and NOP58 as nucleolar markers accross large cell populations. STED microscopy provides nanoscale resolution of sub-nucleolar architecture, allowing us to resolve aberrant clustering of UBF1 and structural disorganization of the nucleolus that are not detectable by conventional microscopy. These imaging approaches are central to linking EWSR1::FLI1-driven nucleolar remodeling to impaired ribosome biogenesis and translational vulnerability in Ewing sarcoma.
